CalendarMetadata.description:
Metadata for a calendar.
Contains essential information about the calendar's type and jurisdiction.

CalendarType.description:
The type of the calendar.
Defines the scope and authority level of the liturgical calendar.

CalendarJurisdiction.description:
The jurisdiction of the calendar.
Determines whether the calendar follows ecclesiastical or civil authority.

ParticularConfig.description:
Configuration options specific to this calendar.
These settings can override or extend the default Romcal configuration or any parent calendar
configuration.

epiphany_on_sunday.description: Epiphany is celebrated on a Sunday

ascension_on_sunday.description: Ascension is celebrated on a Sunday

corpus_christi_on_sunday.description: Corpus Christi is celebrated on a Sunday

DayDefinition.description:
Definition of a liturgical day with all its properties and configurations.
It represents a complete liturgical day definition that can be used
to generate calendar entries with proper precedence, colors, and entity associations.

date_def.description: The date definition for this liturgical day

date_exceptions.description: The date definition exceptions (overrides for specific circumstances)

precedence.description: The precedence type of the liturgical day

commons_def.description:
The **Common** refers to a set of prayers, readings, and chants used for celebrating saints or
feasts that belong to a specific category, such as martyrs, virgins, pastors, or the Blessed
Virgin Mary.

is_holy_day_of_obligation.description:
Holy days of obligation are days on which the faithful are expected to attend Mass
and engage in rest from work and recreation

allow_similar_rank_items.description:
Allow similar items that have the same rank and the same or lower precedence
to coexist with this liturgical day without being overwritten

is_optional.description:
Specify if this liturgical day is optional within a specific liturgical calendar

UNLY #14:
Memorials are either obligatory or optional; their observance is integrated into
the celebration of the occurring weekday in accordance with the norms set forth in the
General Instruction of the Roman Missal and of the Liturgy of the Hours

Note: also used for the dedication of consecrated churches, which is an optional solemnity
that should not overwrite the default weekday.

custom_locale_id.description: The custom locale ID for this date definition in this calendar

entities.description: The entities (Saints, Blessed, or Places) linked from the Entity catalog

titles.description: The combined titles of all entities linked to this date definition

drop.description:
If this liturgical day must be removed from this calendar and from all parent calendars
in the final calendar generated by romcal

colors.description:
The liturgical color(s) of the liturgical day
@deprecated

masses.description: The masses definitions for this liturgical day

DateDef.description:
Date definition supporting various date calculation methods.
Provides flexible ways to specify liturgical dates using different approaches.

date_fn.description: The date function to calculate the base date

anyOf.description: Nth weekday of a specific month

day_of_week.description: The day of the week (0=Sunday, 1=Monday, etc.)

nth_week_in_month.description: Which occurrence of the weekday (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.)

anyOf.description: Last weekday of a specific month

last_day_of_week_in_month.description: The day of the week to find the last occurrence of

anyOf.description: Inherited from the proper of time

MonthIndex.description:
Month index (1-12) with automatic validation

This type ensures that only valid month values are accepted during
deserialization. The value 1 represents January, 2 represents February, etc.

DateFn.description:
Date function for calculating liturgical dates.
Represents movable feasts and special celebrations that require calculation.

DayOfWeek.description:
Day of week (0-6, where 0=Sunday) with automatic validation

This type ensures that only valid day-of-week values are accepted during
deserialization. The value 0 represents Sunday, 1 represents Monday, etc.

DateDefExceptions.description:
Date exceptions that can be either a single exception or multiple exceptions.
Supports both simple single exceptions and complex multiple exception scenarios.

DateDefException.description:
The liturgical day date exception.
Represents a condition and the date to set when that condition is met.

when.description: The condition that triggers the exception

then.description: The date to set when the condition is met

ExceptionCondition.description:
Exception conditions that can trigger a date change.
Defines various conditions under which a date exception applies.

anyOf.description: If the date is between two specified dates

from.description: The start date of the range

to.description: The end date of the range

inclusive.description: Whether the range is inclusive of the start date and the end date

anyOf.description: If the date is the same as another specified date
If the date falls on a specific day of the week

day_of_week.description: The day of the week to match

DateDefExtended.description:
Extended date definition supporting both regular dates and offset dates.
Provides flexibility for date calculations with optional adjustments.

DateDefWithOffset.description:
Date definition with offset for adjustments.
Used when a date needs to be shifted by a specific number of days.

day_offset.description: The number of days to offset the date

Precedence.description:
Liturgical precedence levels for determining which celebration takes priority.
Defines the hierarchical order of liturgical celebrations according to UNLY norms.

CommonDefinition.description:
Common definition for simplified categorization.
Provides a simplified version of the Common enum for easier classification.

EntityPointer.description:
A pointer to an entity in the entity catalog.
Can either reference an existing entity by ID or define a custom entity with additional properties.

anyOf.description: Reference to an existing entity by its ID
Custom entity definition with additional properties specific to a liturgical day

EntityOverride.description:
Custom entity definition that extends or overrides properties from the entity catalog.
Used when a liturgical day needs specific entity properties that differ from the base entity.

id.description: The ID of the entity item (must reference an existing entity in the catalog)

titles.description: The custom titles for this entity in the context of this liturgical day

hide_titles.description: Whether to hide titles when displaying this entity (useful when titles are already included in the entity name)

count.description: The number of persons this entity represents (useful for groups of martyrs or saints)

TitlesDef.description:
Title definition that can be either a simple list or a compound definition.
Supports both direct title lists and compound title operations.

anyOf.description: Compound title definition with append/prepend operations

Title.description:
Titles and patronages associated with saints and blessed.
Represents the various ecclesiastical titles and patronages that can be assigned to entities.

CompoundTitle.description:
Compound title definition for combining multiple titles.
Allows adding titles to the beginning or end of an existing title list.

append.description: The title(s) to add to the end of the existing list of title(s)

prepend.description: The title(s) to add to the beginning of the existing list of title(s)

SaintCount.description:
Represents the number of saints for an entity or a group of entities.

Can be either a specific number (u32) or "MANY" to indicate
an indeterminate number of saints.

# Serialization
- `Number(n)` serializes as integer `n`
- `Many` serializes as string `"MANY"`

# Deserialization
- Integers are converted to `Number(u32)`
- String `"MANY"` is converted to `Many`
- All other types generate an error

Color.description:
Liturgical colors used in the celebration of Mass and other liturgical services.
Each color has specific liturgical significance and is used during particular seasons or celebrations.

oneOf.description: Red - used for martyrs, Pentecost, and Palm Sunday
Rose - used on Gaudete Sunday (3rd Advent) and Laetare Sunday (4th Lent)
Purple - used during Advent and Lent
White - used for Christmas, Easter, and most feasts
Gold - used for solemn celebrations and special occasions
Black - used for funerals and All Souls' Day

MassesDefinitions.description: All mass definitions for a liturgical day

celebration_of_the_passion.description: Celebration of the Passion - special celebration of Christ's passion

chrism_mass.description: Chrism Mass - Mass where holy oils are blessed, typically on Holy Thursday morning

day_mass.description: Day Mass - regular Mass celebrated during the day

easter_vigil.description: Easter Vigil - the most important Mass of the liturgical year, celebrated on Holy Saturday night

evening_mass_of_the_lords_supper.description: Evening Mass of the Lord's Supper - Mass celebrated on Holy Thursday evening

mass_at_dawn.description: Mass at Dawn - Mass celebrated at dawn, particularly on Easter Sunday

mass_of_the_passion.description: Mass of the Passion - Mass focusing on Christ's passion, beginning with the procession with palms

morning_mass.description: Morning Mass - Mass celebrated in the morning

night_mass.description: Night Mass - Mass celebrated during the night hours

previous_evening_mass.description: Previous Evening Mass - Mass celebrated the evening before a major feast

MassCycleDefinition.description: Mass contents for a specific mass time, organized by liturgical cycle

invariant.description: Invariant content that applies to all cycles

year_1.description: Year 1 of the weekday cycle (Cycle I)

year_2.description: Year 2 of the weekday cycle (Cycle II)

year_a.description: Year A of the Sunday cycle

year_a_b.description: Combined years A and B of the Sunday cycle

year_a_c.description: Combined years A and C of the Sunday cycle

year_b.description: Year B of the Sunday cycle

year_b_c.description: Combined years B and C of the Sunday cycle

year_c.description: Year C of the Sunday cycle

MassContent.description:
Content of a mass for a specific liturgical cycle
Maps mass parts (readings, psalms, prayers, antiphons, etc.) to their texts

collect.description: Collect - opening prayer of the Mass

easter_vigil_epistle.description: Epistle - reading from the epistles (Easter Vigil)

entrance_antiphon.description: Entrance Antiphon - opening chant of the Mass

messianic_entry.description: Messianic entry reading (during the procession with palms, before the Mass of the Passion)

prayer_over_the_offerings.description: Prayer over the Offerings - prayer during the offertory

prayer_over_the_people.description: Prayer over the People - blessing over the congregation

preface.description: Preface - introduction to the Eucharistic Prayer

reading_1.description: Reading 1 - first reading (usually from the Old Testament)

reading_2.description: Reading 2 - second reading (usually from the New Testament)

sequence.description: Sequence - special chant on certain feasts

solemn_blessing.description: Solemn Blessing - special blessing on certain occasions
